78027.subject: How big is America’s “obesity penalty”?
78027.body:
The Economist’s week ahead

Автор: The Economist


Автор: The Economist

    
    
    Прочитайте цю статтю на LinkedIn, щоб приєднатися до обговорення

Sign up for free here to receive this newsletter in your inbox every Saturday. You’ll also get our weekly newsletter with an exclusive introduction from our top editors. Weight-loss drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy are not just having an impact on obesity. They hold promise as treatments for heart disease, addiction and myriad other health problems.  Their growing popularity is changing society, too. American data show striking consequences for women’s careers. The “obesity penalty” on income, a long-known phenomenon that exists for women but not men, might soon disappear. Slavea Chankova, Health-care correspondent Editor's picks How big is America’s “obesity penalty”? GLP-1s offer a rare insight into the social and economic effects of carrying extra weight A world map of childhood obesity More children today are obese than underweight. Which countries are worst affected?  Weight-loss drugs are spreading across the world The expiry of patents in China, India and elsewhere will boost uptake dramatically Should you microdose GLP-1 drugs for weight loss? Possibly. But only under medical supervision Is obesity a disease? It wasn’t. But it is now It’s not just obesity. Drugs like Ozempic will change the world As they become cheaper, they promise to improve billions of lives Go beyond the headlines Get unlimited digital access to The Economist by subscribing today.
